### Run 0001 — AF — Afghanistan — 2026-09-06T20:25:08Z

- Start: 2026-09-06T20:25:08Z. End: 2026-09-06T20:33:58Z. Sweep: 1. Final status: **partial**.
- Catalog at search time: 45 AF-assigned feeds; 0 AF supplemental records. Neither file was modified.
- Evaluated: **17 candidate station/service records** (Killid regional leads grouped as one unresolved network record). **2 ready for catalog review; 2 already present; 12 need verification; 1 endpoint excluded.** Counts total 17.
- Performed **12 endpoint probes: 8 passed, 4 failed**. The eight passes include the existing Srood feed and two URLs for the same Salam Watandar feed; they are not eight new stations. Six distinct, previously uncataloged feeds passed; two have sufficient identity/country evidence for catalog review, and four remain on hold for attribution/provenance.
- All sources below accessed or attempted on 2026-09-06. No browser decoding, listening/content recognition, or worldwide-availability claim is made.

#### Search scope and evidence

Searched English, Dari and Pashto text for national/public, commercial, local/community, women-led and educational radio. Searched for university radio and Uzbek/Turkmen services, but obtained no independently verified distinct stream in those categories. Followed official broadcasters and parent organizations, regional Killid leads, Radio Browser, Boorjal and AfghanStream. This is a substantial first pass, not an exhaustive station census.

Source access and useful evidence:

- [Ariana FM](https://ariana.fm/) HTML supplied the Radio.co live-feed URL; [ATN about](https://www.arianatelevision.com/about-atn/) confirms Kabul ownership/location. The actual feed probe returned 403.
- [Begum operator projects](https://begum.ngo/our-projects) links [Begum FM](https://www.begum.fm/) and [Jawanan FM](https://www.jawanan.fm/). The operator confirms Begum's Kabul origin and Dari/Pashto programming; Jawanan's official homepage explicitly says it broadcasts from Kabul, and local HTML contains Pashto program metadata. Those are distinct services. Begum embeds `https://embed.radio.co/player/db2e3dd.js`; Jawanan embeds `https://embed.radio.co/player/94f3945.js`. Both embedded-script fetches returned 403, so exact feed URLs were obtained from directory player metadata rather than those scripts. This provenance limitation remains visible for catalog review.
- [Boorjal](https://boorjal.com/radios/) HTML contains base64-encoded public player configuration, decoded as JSON; it provided the tested domestic/uncertain-origin feeds and the duplicate BBC URL. Its labels are leads, not proof of station origin. About-page fetches failed.
- [AfghanStream](https://afghanstream.tv/) public page configuration independently supplied Begum and Ariana URLs, a second Salam URL, Afghan Beats, ATN News HLS and Srood. Its displayed online status and audience counters were not used as validation evidence.
- [Radio Browser AF query](https://de1.api.radio-browser.info/json/stations/bycountrycodeexact/AF) returned 124 records. Examined the response for relevant station identities; many listings have unrelated international names/homepages. The project likewise has apparently unrelated entries in its AF category. These are **attribution concerns, not an audited count of incorrect records**. No baseline records were removed. Exact original/final URLs were compared globally against current catalog and supplements; relevant names were checked as secondary evidence. Similar names alone were not merged.
- [Salam Watandar](https://swn.af/) and its [radio page](https://swn.af/radio-stream/) were readable through web retrieval; direct HTML access returned 403. An [operator document indexed at ACBAR](https://download.acbar.org/files/files/1524374801.pdf) names its Kabul station, but opening the PDF failed; it remains supporting indexed evidence, not a completed document read.
- [Taleem-ul-Islam's self-described official profile](https://www.linkedin.com/company/taleemulislam) supplies Kandahar and regional frequencies; official website fetches at [taleemulislam.net](https://www.taleemulislam.net/) returned 403. Ownership/profile and stream binding are held for verification.
- [Spogmai official page](https://www.spogmairadio.com/) was readable through web retrieval but local HTML returned 403; the [developer's app description](https://apps.apple.com/zm/app/spogmai-fm/id1448869097) supplies Kabul/Kandahar and Pashto context. Directory stream is 404.
- [Arman](https://arman.fm/), [its tune-in page](https://arman.fm/tune-in/) and [MOBY owner profile](https://mobygroup.com/businesses/channels-and-platforms/arman-fm) establish Afghan identity; no current direct stream was exposed in retrieved text, which still describes Flash. A similarly named California website is a separate lead and was not substituted.
- [Killid](https://tkg.af/) and [radios page](https://tkg.af/radios/) returned 403. An [indexed historical operator release](https://pajhwok.com/wp-content/uploads/old/TKG%20press%20Release%20about%20launching%20RK%20streaming%20%28English%29.pdf) lists seven local stations; opening the PDF failed. Retain these as historical leads. [Herat directory listing](https://onlineradiobox.com/af/killidherat/?lang=en) and [Kabul stream listing](https://netplayer.net/radio/radio-killid-36218/listen) appeared in search results; neither is current operation proof.
- [RTA](https://rta.af/) and [about](https://rta.af/about) yielded no useful player in parsed text/current shell; [legacy RTA](https://legacy.rta.af/) and the [official app listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?hl=en_US&id=com.rta.media) are next-visit leads. [Shamshad](https://www.shamshadtv.tv/) appeared in searches, but a distinct direct radio feed was not established.
- [Meraj operator](https://sakena.org/tv-meraj/) confirms Herat radio and links [radiomeraj.af](https://radiomeraj.af/), whose certificate has expired. [Mursal](https://radiomursal.com/) failed TLS hostname validation. [Hurriyat](https://hurriyat.af/) failed fetches; [its developer app listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.hurriyat.radioapp) and public YouTube live search results remain leads. No TLS/access restrictions were bypassed.
- [Afghan Beats claimed official site](https://afghanbeatsradio.com/) could not be opened. [Srood](https://radiosrood.com/) confirms an Afghan-music brand but did not establish broadcasting location in retrieved text. External services found in directories (Azadi, VOA, Deewa, Mashal and Afghanistan International) were retained as future attribution leads rather than treated as domestic Afghan stations.

Initial sandboxed network access failed DNS resolution. The authorized public-page fetches and bounded probes subsequently ran with network access; those results below are actual network results, not the initial sandbox failures. Runtime scratch copies are in `/tmp/radio-af-research/`; all durable conclusions, URLs and probe evidence are recorded in this ledger and do not depend on those temporary files.

#### Next visit and handoff

- Recheck the two proposed feeds and confirm official player-to-stream mapping if the embed scripts become accessible. Revisit Taleem-ul-Islam and Salam Watandar first-party configuration and attribution before promoting them.
- Establish Boorjal and Afghan Beats' actual country of operation; public HTTPS audio alone cannot resolve domestic/diaspora classification.
- Follow the six regional Killid leads independently, recover Spogmai and Arman's current players, inspect RTA's public radio metadata, and revisit Meraj, Mursal and Hurriyat when their sites are accessible. Do not substitute television or on-demand lesson files for live radio.

[Radiovlora.com](https://www.radiovlora.com/) now combines hosting sales with a Rinia-named mount; linkage to the licensed local station is uncertain. [Radio Star](https://radiostar.al/) returned a sample page, not a current stream.
- [Dodona app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?hl=en&id=com.radyododona882.radyododona882_app), [operator about](https://radiododona.com/per-ne/) and [partner listing](https://www.evropaelire.org/radio/affiliates/info/184/1108) distinguish Kosovo’s Dodona from Albania’s Bektashi service. [Fontana’s own about page](https://radiofontana.org/rreth-nesh/) places that search result in Kosovo. No separate-country search run was undertaken.
- [University of Vlora report](https://univlora.edu.al/media/dokument/uv-raport-vetevleresimi-2026.pdf) surfaced a multimedia lab, not an established live stream. [Mother Teresa University publication](https://unt.edu.mk/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Revista-studentore-UNT-studenti-Nr.2-2021.pdf) refers to Radio Studenti in Skopje. No absence-of-stations claim follows from these searches.

Duplicate checks used original/final URLs across the full catalog and supplements, relevant name matches, prior ledger evidence, and Radiojar mount equivalence across shards/temporary query tokens. Existing entries are recorded below without recertifying their original country labels. There were no earlier AL findings. No browser decoding, audio content recognition or worldwide availability test was performed.

URLs and evidence for remaining individually evaluated sources appear below. Directory/app search snippets are leads, not primary identity proof.
- Public artist pages https://sansal.simdif.com/ and https://GhorbaDz.Simdif.com/ were retrieved, but the stream association remains absent. Radio Browser’s Radiojar URL variants were retained as unresolved provenance rather than promoted to Radio Algérie Coran.
- Access failures: webradio.tda.dz DNS failure; radio-dzair.com/www timeouts; radio-dzair.net DNS failure; both Hawana website spellings DNS failures; Hawana Facebook unreadable; Annaba Chaabi public page/stream 404; act-bouzeguene.org DNS failure; Tis Snat iframe 404. Idurar player redirects to a domain-sale page. These are observed access outcomes, not proof that the broadcasters have ceased all operations.
- Deduplication: all candidate probe original/final URLs checked against the full catalog and supplements; host/path canonical checks additionally ignore trailing slash/query differences. No probe matched any existing URL or earlier ledger URL. A global name scan found no matching proposed named service. Generic Jow live/live1 are held pending programme-identity comparison. No decoding, listening identification or worldwide/browser availability claim is made.
- Unknown language arrays are deliberately empty in proposals; channel names, a page language and server geography are not sufficient to invent language lists or studio coordinates. Current genres beyond directly identified music, news, educational or local services can be enriched during integration.

#### Sources and findings

- Official South Seas sources retrieved: https://www.southseasbroadcasting.com/history/, /93khj/, /v103/, /1047beat/ and /kkhjhd2/ (all on that same HTTPS host). Operator history establishes Tafuna facilities, local brands and KNWJ’s 2019 conversion to KKBT. V103 detailed primary profile: https://www.southseasbroadcasting.com/platforms/v-103.
- Official listen links map to `https://www.southseasbroadcasting.com?streamplayer=` IDs 99933 (93KHJ), 99939 (V103), 99938 (Beat), 99940 (Oldies). Curl returned 403 for all four; plugin player script also returned 403. An ordinary in-app browser successfully loaded the 99933 URL as the operator homepage, but the displayed page did not expose the live player. No challenge/access-control bypass was used. The station pages were readable.
- Stream discovery for those four: https://listenonlineradio.com/as/93khj, https://listenonlineradio.com/as/v103, https://listenonlineradio.com/as/104-7-the-beat, https://listenonlineradio.com/as/oldies-93-7. Each directory page explicitly labels its direct SecureNetSystems mount with the matching station. Primary-source identity/country and current transport checks support review readiness; official player-to-mount corroboration and audible station identification remain useful integration checks.
- Additional player sources opened: https://worldradiomap.com/as/play/kkhj_live, https://www.reymod.com/radios/american-samoa/93khj, https://onlineradiobox.com/as/, https://onlineradiobox.com/as/kkhjhd2/, https://onlineradiobox.com/as/wvuv/, https://onlineradiobox.com/as/kkbt/. The last two generic paths did not reveal station audio. ReyMod’s selected source was the operator HTML homepage, not an audio stream; unrelated recommended-station URLs in that page were ignored.
- Island Rhythm redirects to https://islandpraise.live/ and both fetched homepages contain the same direct Asura audio element. Current primary page establishes American Samoa address and current brand. Search-cached https://islandrhythm.live/about-us/ describes KKAS-LP and its founder, while a fresh request to that path returns 404; it is historical context, not an asserted current biography.
- Religious/community sources: official K-Love KVPP station finder; FCC historical KGIF/KIOE/KULA-LP notices; Streema KMOA, KPPO, KGIF/KULA historical leads; https://zeno.fm/radio/kmoa-fm89-7/ and https://zeno.fm/radio/kmoa-fm-89-7/. Zeno public page metadata exposes the two mount URLs recorded below. Neither passes; no query/token manipulation or insecure retry was attempted.
- KSBS official domain returned an error page; www.905kppofm.org, secondsamoan.org and www.teenchallengeamericansamoa.org failed DNS. Legacy www.khjradio.com and www.wvuv.com failed TLS. These are observed access outcomes, not a conclusion that all affected stations are off air.
- Territorial attribution: Remnant, Eyespy/HAMO, Talofa, Malo and Magik were investigated only far enough to establish that AS directory placement conflicts with independent Samoa evidence; their full research belongs to the WS turn. Antenna Web and Station Beta remain uncertain rather than assigned a country by branding.
- NOAA primary source https://www.weather.gov/ppg/nwr establishes two local weather transmitters but does not supply a direct online audio feed. Government KVZK source describes television; no unsupported KVZK-FM radio addition was made.
- Deduplication checked candidate original/resolved URLs, then hostname/path canonical equivalents against the complete catalog and supplements, plus prior ledger mentions. Name/call-sign search found the Oldies UM record and existing national K-Love feeds. Existing 181FM parameterized directory variants were collapsed by host/path without requesting their HTTP URLs. No proposed ID/URL collides with catalog or supplemental records.
- Probe results show point-in-time MIME/audio-byte availability from this computer; no decoding, on-air listening identification, continuous uptime or worldwide/browser availability claim is made. No exact studio coordinates or unverified language lists were invented.

## Run 0006 — Andorra (`AD`)

- Started: 2026-09-07T01:28:05.944553+00:00
- Ended: 2026-09-07T01:37:54.095312+00:00
- Status: **partial** — useful commercial/local additions verified; public HLS, inactive/uncertain internet services and local relay distinctions remain.
- Baseline: 6 catalog feeds; 0 AD supplements. Fresh Radio Browser AD response contained 12 records including three identical Polignano URLs.
- Results: **48 discovery records; 8 ready for catalog review; 9 already present; 24 needs verification; 7 excluded**. Records include alternate endpoint/duplicate/history leads and are not a count of unique broadcasters.
- Checks: 18 actual bounded probes, 10 passed. Two of the failures were accidental truncated plugin-asset paths from URL extraction, not station endpoints; retained transparently below. Thus 16 real stream/playlist checks, 10 passes, of which 8 are new verified candidates and 2 are stale directory endpoints withheld.
- No catalog, supplement, release or website changes. Proposed records remain review material.

### Scope and evidence

Searches covered Catalan, English, Spanish, French and Portuguese wording; public RTVA, local commercial operators, network branches, diocesan/community/university leads, internet-only and diaspora services. The official [Cadena Pirenaica network page](https://www.cadenapirenaica.com/web/cadena-pirenaica-radio-i-televisio/radio/) distinguishes owned stations from distributed parent networks. RadioMap lists imported French/Spanish services, including NRJ, Radio France, RNE, Catalunya Ràdio, Tele-Taxi, Kiss and Pyrénées FM; reception in Andorra alone does not justify copying their national feeds into AD. No separate university/community station was established by the relevant queries; this is a search limitation, not proof of absence.

Critical endpoint corrections: Valira official `/8378/stream` replaces stale directory `/8022/stream`; Pròxima official `/8400/stream` replaces directory `/8058/stream`; RAC1 official `/8384/stream` works while Valira’s embedded legacy IP endpoint fails. Auxiliary header reads at 2026-09-07T01:31:52Z returned `icy-name: RVALIRA` for `/8378`, `Emisoras ABC` for `/8022`, `RadioCaster Stream` and example.com for `/8058`, and blank name for Clàssics. Header reads were bounded to five seconds; they supplement, not replace, the stricter probes.

[Flaix legal identification](https://flaixandorra.com/ca/avis-legal/) explicitly names Andorra1 Clàssics and its Andorra la Vella operator. [SER contact](https://cadenaser.com/radio-ser-principat-d-andorra/contacto/) supplies local address. [Valira anniversary](https://radiovalira.ad/aniversari/) supplies current local history. [Bondia’s 2018 event report](https://www.bondia.ad/societat/la-mostra-internacional-de-folklore-omple-el-complex-sociocultural) is secondary corroboration for already-present Ondas de Portugal, not a fresh primary verification.

Global duplicate checks compare original and resolved URLs against the full current catalog plus supplements, normalize default ports/trailing slashes, and check prior ledger URL mentions. Names and StreamTheWorld mount identifiers were also searched globally; no matching existing/new proposed identity was found for the eight ready records. Exact probe/dedup output is preserved below. No generic parent stream is treated as a local service solely because it can be heard in Andorra.

Imported `probe_endpoint` without running the full refresh. Successful results mean valid TLS, public-address pinning, HTTPS-only redirects, HTTP 200/206, supported audio MIME and 4,096 sample bytes. No browser decoding or worldwide availability claim. Status 0 is generic transport failure; do not infer geo-blocking, permanent closure or a particular TLS error. KW’s insecure stream was never requested. HLS manifests were checked only for compatibility; no segment conversion was performed.

- Ended: 2026-09-07T02:43:04.907636+00:00
- Status: **partial**. National/regional, commercial, faith, community, cultural and educational services covered; failed endpoints, small operators and historical/diaspora attribution still need follow-up.
- Baseline: 8 AO catalog feeds, no AO supplements. Fresh Radio Browser response: 19 records. Rádios Angola directory: 52 station cards across three pages. RNA official player index: 27 distinct named feeds.
- Results: **100 discovery records; 44 ready for catalog review; 12 already present; 42 needs verification; 2 excluded**. Alternate endpoints and historical leads are records, not unique broadcaster totals.
- Checks: **71 distinct endpoint probes; 54 passed**. RNA: 21/27 pass including already-present Rádio Luanda; six return 404. Passing audio alone does not establish station identity.
- No catalog/supplement/release/site changes. Proposed JSON is review material only.

### Coverage and provenance

[RNA’s live index](https://rna.ao/) and [legacy official index](https://rna.ao/rna.ao/) expose all 27 feed/name pairs. The [network description](https://rna.ao/rna.ao/quem-somos/) documents national, provincial and municipal services and multiple languages. Language arrays remain empty for provincial/multilingual feeds where per-station language lists were not established; empty does not mean no speech. Ngola Yetu’s national-language remit is corroborated by a [current broadcaster article](https://rna.ao/rna.ao/2026/05/25/radio-ngola-yetu-afirma-se-como-simbolo-de-inclusao-e-unidade-nacional/). Preserve official player names such as Cuando Cubango as broadcaster labels; administrative-boundary changes were not independently audited or used to invent new feeds.

Commercial checks followed public station HTML, embedded BRLogic/Maxcast/VOXHD/SonicPanel players and directly linked audio. [Mais’s primary live page](https://radiomais.ao/emissao-online/) confirms all five regional services; it was readable through the web reader despite direct curl 403 responses. Their direct URLs came from Rádios Angola and passed current checks. [D’Agosto’s official app listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=br.com.portalradios.dagosto) corroborates Luanda origin. CEFOJOR, UnIA and UNIC supplied educational leads; church/operator sites supplied faith services. Self-managed Zeno profiles provide declared provenance for internet-only stations, not independently verified studio coordinates.

Every proposed original and resolved URL was compared globally against catalog, supplements and prior ledger. Canonical checks account for default ports/trailing slash and Zeno/surfernetwork mount aliases while preserving original URLs for use. No proposed duplicate was found. Zango FM’s passing stream matches existing Radio Zango FM (`dbf8eb93-1aac-4df2-9e67-2d03d08b1deb`), currently labeled US, after ignoring its tracking query. Its official about/contact pages support a proposed US→AO correction; it is excluded from new additions and no catalog change was made. Similar names alone do not prove duplication; suspected alternates stay held. A stale directory Muzangala RadioKing URL is already catalogued as A2Z RADIO (BD), so it is not adopted for Angola. Current official Muzangala instead uses the listen2myradio URL below. MFM’s stale directory endpoint returns 401 while its official endpoint passes. Nosso Tempo has two passing paths; only the exact official path is proposed. Rádio 8000’s widget ID 8042 resolves to audio port 7020; both were inspected rather than inferred.

## Run 0008 — Anguilla (`AI`)

- Started: 2026-09-07T03:26:55.818810+00:00
- Ended: 2026-09-07T03:36:48.497448+00:00
- Status: **partial** — national/public, private, faith, community, new digital services, historical stations and directory anomalies covered; unresolved operators and country assignments remain.
- Baseline: two AI catalog feeds; no AI supplements. Fresh Radio Browser response: six records. Broader directories and official sites supplied additional leads.
- Results: **34 evaluated records; 4 ready for catalog review; 6 already present; 23 needs verification; 1 excluded**. Records include alternates and historical leads, not unique-station totals.
- Actual checks: **19 distinct HTTPS endpoint probes; 10 passed**. Successful audio alone does not establish origin.
- Catalog, supplements and website unchanged. Proposed records below are review material.

### Primary evidence and coverage

[Government’s Radio Anguilla service page](https://dls.gov.ai/service/radio-anguilla) establishes the national broadcaster and its official website. [UpBeat’s about page](https://ubr977.com/about/) identifies its Anguillan history; its homepage gives a Rey Hill address. [Kool’s website](https://koolfm103.ai/) identifies its North Side studio and exposes its exact player. Radio Anguilla and Kool use base64-encoded public player configuration, decoded as data without executing page code.

[NBR Grace’s own site](https://newbeginningradio.org/) names the station and embeds its live player. Its local provenance is corroborated by [CANARI/DNR’s primary Anguilla community survey](https://canari.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Darwin-Sargassum-OTs-Communication-Engagement-Strategy-final.pdf), PDF page 51, and [local reporting on the broadcaster’s Christmas contest](https://theanguillian.com/2020/01/nbr-christmas-solo-competition-a-phenomenal-event/). The current website is under construction, so exact studio-address metadata remains unspecified. English is used for the four proposals; no claim that every programme is exclusively English. Spanish-language discovery found historical bilingual programming but no additional verified feed.

Global duplicate checks compared original and successful final URLs with every catalog/supplement entry and earlier ledger URLs, including MyRadioStream path/port aliases, cache-query variations and Zeno/surfernetwork mount aliases. Original stream strings and all emitted query parameters are preserved. Four proposed feeds have no such matches. Two Antenna Web village URLs both resolve to an existing global feed; a dedicated geographic landing page does not prove local origin. iHeart’s own station list supports correcting the existing WRNO-HD2 country from AI to US. No correction was applied.

### Actual endpoint and duplicate checks

Imported `probe_endpoint` without invoking catalog refresh. Passing checks require HTTPS with valid TLS on every hop, public-address pinning, HTTP 200/206, supported MP3/AAC/Ogg MIME and 4,096 audio sample bytes. Existing helper request/connect timeouts bound each check. HTTP-listed feeds were tested only as same-host/port/path HTTPS upgrades; no insecure audio requested. Status 0 means generic connection failure, not proof of closure or a specific TLS problem. No browser decoding or worldwide availability claim. Public session and cache parameters were preserved; no authentication or access-control workaround. Temporary signed Zeno final URLs are evidence only.

### Findings and primary evidence

[Radio Nacional’s homepage](https://www.radionacional.com.ar/) links its [dedicated LRA36 player](https://www.radionacional.com.ar/reproductor/reproductor_lra36_n2.php). [Argentina’s joint command](https://www.argentina.gob.ar/estado-mayor-conjunto/sonidos-de-la-antartida) establishes Base Esperanza broadcasting and offers program archives. [Fundación Marambio](https://marambio.aq/radioarcangelsangabriel.html) describes the 2023 encoder replacement and station programming. The [older VMF player](https://vmf.edge-apps.net/embed/live.php?streamname=sc_rad32-100131&autoplay=true) still supplies the same failed sc_rad32 audio URL. A [Radio Addict lead](https://www.radio-addict.com/en/stream-rhxLw4ANWDBnnXCmkjLb8W/listen-Radio-Nacional-Arcangel-San-Gabriel-LRA-36-Antartida) was fetched but no usable alternate direct endpoint was established. A failed Internet endpoint does not prove the FM or shortwave service is closed.

[Ice Radio’s former DJ](https://www.pgc.umn.edu/news/qa-jay-dickson-pgc-director/) and a [Scott Base firsthand account](https://www.annikaandresen.com/antarcticablog/the-social-side-of-scott-base) establish local radio activity, but do not provide a fresh public stream. Historical base station details from [Radio Heritage](https://www.radioheritage.com/story135/) are retained as leads, not current operation claims. [AWI’s monitoring description](https://www.awi.de/en/science/climate-sciences/physical-oceanography/main-research-focus/ocean-acoustics-group/awi-ocean-acoustics-group-passive-acoustic-monitoring.html) distinguishes former PALAOA live acquisition from later offline recordings.

[A’Net Station’s current listen playlist](https://www.anetstation.com/MP3/ANETSTATIONDOTCOM.m3u) is a list of individual recordings; its [about page](https://www.anetstation.com/about.htm) and sub-Antarctic homepage do not resolve current location. [Muzaiko’s official site](https://muzaiko.info/) supplies a working audio feed but no Antarctic location evidence. [Urbana Play’s official contact](https://urbanaplayfm.com/contacto/) explicitly identifies Buenos Aires, contradicting its [Antarctica directory listing](https://www.allradio.net/radio/25464). [Chile’s Air Force](https://fach.mil.cl/iv-brigada-aerea-difunde-actividades-del-mes-del-aire-y-del-espacio-en-0) places the Soberanía 94.1 namesake in Punta Arenas.

### Limits and next visit

Searches covered Argentine, US, New Zealand, Chilean, Australian and British base radio, historical public/community services, international web stations and Russian-language name leads. Search results and historical station names cannot establish exhaustive coverage or current operation. No public endpoint was found for several local FM services. French, Indian, Chinese and other national program base entertainment remain possible future leads; communications radio must be distinguished from broadcast programming. Revisit LRA36 during documented live programming and inspect its current official player; seek current primary internet-player evidence for Ice Radio, Scott Base and Soberanía 90.5. Verify the true origins of the six existing AQ catalog feeds and Muzaiko before any catalog integration. FunkyUncleFm and Soberanía site fetches timed out; some web opens returned cache misses. This was a live search with documented unresolved leads, not a claim that Antarctica has no online stations.

The checkpoint above was saved before finalization. Full candidate decisions and probe evidence are durable in this ledger; temporary fetches/scripts are in `/tmp/radio-aq-research`. No catalog, supplement, build, release or publication was changed.

### Search coverage and source handling

Covered public/national ABS; commercial networks; community/talk; Christian, Adventist, Catholic and Anglican stations; internet-only services; English and Spanish-language leads; university-station searches; and explicit Barbuda/Codrington leads. No separately verified Barbuda-only stream emerged. Abundant Life's historical Codrington studio needs a current operator/player check.

Radio Browser, Dadli Directory, Caribbean Radio, RadioStationWorld, Listen Online Radio, Live Online Radio, RadioInc, RadioSpinner, Streema, TuneIn and Zeno provided discovery. Operator sites, publisher material, station apps and primary player configuration supplied identity or endpoint evidence where specified. Directory labels are never primary country proof. The Antigua museum newsletter's station list is explicitly Google-compiled and was not used as independent primary evidence. The sources arrays below record consulted evidence URLs; some were available only through the search index and access failures are stated. Unvisited links merely suggested by pages are not claimed as read.

Public player paths resolved: ZDK/WTP/Nice/So Arise direct HTML audio; Jump SecureNetSystems stable streamSrcDB; Lighthouse official embed → public stationSettings → stable streamSrcDB; ABS official radio page → Voscast key player → explicit 9345 HTTPS endpoint; Pointe official SAM widget station 126837 → public station metadata identifying Pointe FM and SP_R3743588 → directory HTTPS variant of that same mount. Public player session/config data unrelated to station evidence was not copied into the ledger. The old Caribbean Radio playlist nostream.mp3 fallback is not a station and was not tested or proposed.

### Duplicate review, limitations and next visit

Original and final URLs were compared globally against the current catalog, supplements and all earlier ledger runs. Comparison normalizes default ports, trailing slashes and percent encoding; Zeno host variants are grouped, and StreamTheWorld pool hosts and codec suffixes are compared by mount. Query-free keys are used conservatively for duplicate review only: actual source/probe/proposed URLs retain their parameters unchanged. All nine ready candidates have no existing feed-key or previous ledger URL match. Station names were also reviewed in context; a shared name/frequency alone does not establish duplicate programming. Separate unresolved Rogers/Twin Island and Sun/Jump relationships are documented rather than asserted. Unprobed leads have no completed URL duplicate check and are not ready.

Operator access gaps included Observer 403, some guessed listen/contact paths 404, former station domains displaying unrelated content, Vibz/DNECA timeouts, Priest Isaac TLS handshake failure, and Zoom challenge HTML. Late in the run, requests to several unrelated source hosts all returned curl DNS error 6, including previously reachable Zeno; this may be an environment/network interruption rather than simultaneous domain closures. New lead fetches were stopped after that cluster, and the successful earlier audio checks remain timestamped historical observations. Primary South Leeward Conference identity text was available through live search results while direct retrieval failed. Second Advent's secure endpoint is corroborated by directory players; primary ownership of that exact radio.co account should be reconfirmed at integration.

On the next AG sweep: recover current Observer/Hitz/Flava direct players; revisit Abundant Life and Codrington with a current church source; resolve Catholic Radio's current public player and Healthy Choice's Streann radio configuration; establish Rum Bus's actual operator location; follow Consushness/Viva and remaining directory labels once DNS is functioning; verify Rogers/Twin Island and Sun/Jump history; find current English Harbour/Platinum/Variety/DNECA feeds; revisit university/community searches and Spanish UnoRadio. Review the La Senda country correction separately. No finding here proves that a held station is off air or that the country's discovery is exhaustive.

The 250-entry checklist, including PS, EH and XK, and the summary/run counts were validated. Earlier logs and this run's checkpoint were preserved. Durable candidate identities, sources, endpoint results and proposed records are above; temporary HTML and scripts are under `/tmp/radio-ag-research`. Catalog, supplements, builds and publication were unchanged.

### Final results — completed 2026-09-07T06:45:58.737884+00:00

- Finished attempt: partial; Runs incremented once. 129 candidate/identity records evaluated: 19 ready for catalog review, 70 already present, 39 needing verification, 1 excluded.
- Fresh Radio Browser inventory: 1,238 AR rows using limit=100000. The first default request returned 1,000 and was replaced by the complete request; the complete result was below the requested limit. This inventory is not a claim that all 1,238 received primary-source research. 35 university/community/provincial directory rows were specifically screened and retained within candidate evidence below.
- Primary Radio Nacional pass: 53 service players; 45 direct endpoints already cataloged, 8 absent endpoints probed, 6 of those passing and 2 returning 404. LRA36 Base Esperanza belongs to the existing AQ research entry and was not researched/probed again here. LRA10's Ushuaia location remains Argentina despite its station name mentioning Islas Malvinas; no geographic assignment was inferred from a name alone.
- 64 actual endpoint attempts across 61 distinct URLs: 36 successful attempts and 28 failed attempts. Three repeated community-grid URLs produced additional attempts; all actual results are preserved, while candidate/proposal counts are deduplicated.
- Catalog baseline: 843 AR feeds; no AR supplements. No catalog or supplemental changes, build, release or publication.
- Next country: Armenia (`AM`).

### Search coverage and evidence handling

This pass covered Radio Nacional's linked domestic/thematic players, the ARUNA university network, Buenos Aires/Santa Cruz/Corrientes/Misiones provincial leads, the Cadena 3 commercial group, FARCO and COMECUCO community networks, Mapuche/Qom/Tartagal Indigenous radio leads, Catholic Radio María and internet/video-oriented Futurock/Vorterix. Spanish and English searches were used, with Indigenous names and accented spelling variants. Current on-air language lists were not inferred from ethnicity. RAE is recorded as an Argentina-origin external service. Radio programs, podcasts, static sample files and TV embeds are distinguished from continuous radio streams.

Official player metadata was inspected without authentication. Inovanex public player code calls its anonymous configuration endpoint using values already embedded in the broadcaster's public iframe; the returned domain/port and documented proxy construction were used for Antena Libre and Universidad CALF. No access controls were bypassed. UNJu's HTML-encoded audio settings, UNLaR's public wpRadio configuration, UNSa's linked player, UNLP's separate AM/FM players and COMECUCO's member/grid audio elements supplied exact endpoints. Source/probe URLs retain their published query parameters. Network sandbox DNS errors at the beginning were resolved by authorized external public reads; they are not station failures. Some individual pages still failed as documented.

### Duplicate review and next visit

Compared original and resolved endpoints globally against catalog, supplements and earlier run logs. Canonical review groups percent-encoding/default-port/trailing-slash variants, StreamTheWorld pool hosts/format suffixes and case-normalized mounts, Radio Nacional Magma host/port variants, and Inovanex's documented /:port/stream proxy form with its port-based equivalent. Query-free keys are conservative duplicate-review keys only; actual URLs are not rewritten. This caught existing Kermés, La Uni, Universidad CALF and Cadena group variants. Multiple Radio María alternatives remain one service. Every ready record has a current passing probe, primary country/identity evidence and no prior feed match. Similar names alone do not establish duplicate programming. The directory's generic UNLP sample MP3 was excluded; UNLP's actual AM/FM are distinct official services.

This is a partial national pass, not an exhaustive inventory of Argentina. Next visit should inspect the remaining Radio Browser rows by province and operator rather than a popularity quota, pursue the seven FARCO additions, expand ARUNA beyond the member links visible on its homepage, and cover municipal/low-power/rural and minority-language stations more deeply. Revisit Río Turbio/Puerto Iguazú, UNQ 503, failed Cuyo mounts, UNLaM's obsolete player variants, UNAJ/UNLa 410 responses, San Juan/Rosario/Provincial site restrictions, UNDAV and Estación Sur audio players, and current Petü/Puel Mapu/Qom/Tartagal online feeds. Futurock's HLS-only evidence needs a supported official direct alternative. Vorterix's current homepage primarily exposes video. Unreachable pages and endpoints do not prove a station is off air. The initial default Radio Browser cap was corrected; remaining primary-source coverage, not a directory count limit, is the main gap.

Useful source collections: [ARUNA](https://aruna.cin.edu.ar/), [FARCO member map](https://farco.redelivre.org.br/), [COMECUCO live grid](https://comecuco.org/radio-en-vivo/), [ENACOM community-station location account](https://www.enacom.gob.ar/institucional/capacitacion-de-fomeca-en-la-ciudad-de-godoy-cruz_n4606), and [UNGS network overview](https://www.ungs.edu.ar/new/la-uni-radio-en-vivo-por-streaming). Direct fetches additionally included Radio Nacional's homepage and /emisoras/, FARCO's homepage, COMECUCO's homepage and individual member pages cited above, broadcaster institutional pages and the linked public player resources. Some guessed paths returned 404 and are not treated as authoritative station closure evidence; www.radios.com.ar and the guessed Barriletes domain did not resolve. Detailed candidates and probes are durable here; temporary public HTML/configuration and scripts are under `/tmp/radio-ar-research`.

Validated the 250 unique country/territory checklist entries, including PS/EH/XK; preserved earlier logs and this run's checkpoint; updated summary, counts and next-country rotation. Catalog and supplemental hashes were unchanged.

### Duplicate review, source access and next visit

Compared every discovered original and resolved audio URL globally against current catalog, supplements and all earlier ledger runs, using exact URLs and conservative query-free, default-port, percent-decoded and trailing-slash review keys. Stream4cast eu/eu1 proxy pool names are grouped by account/path. Review keys do not rewrite actual playback URLs. Existing eight AM feeds are recorded as already present, including four country-provenance concerns. The global Quran feed was seen in earlier country research and was not added. Similar Energy FM, Radio Jazz FM and Radio Jan names elsewhere were reviewed without merging unrelated services by name. Distinct public-radio mounts were retained as different services; transmitter-frequency lists were not expanded into fictitious feeds.

Primary public-radio pages were readable through the web tool, while curl returned 403; its JavaScript-only player exposed no station list in web text. The English listening page retains apparently historical transmission information, so it was not treated as a fresh FM or geopolitical coverage inventory. The current Armenian page names First Programme, Im Radio and Arevik. Radio Culture remains held for primary channel-to-mount confirmation. The historical armradioplayer.online domain is now offered for sale, and imradio.am redirects to a mostly empty spyurk.fm WordPress page; neither proves a station has closed. Jazz FM contacts were available through indexed primary-page retrieval despite current direct-server 500 responses. Aurora/Kiss/Roks audio 403 responses were not bypassed. Radio Jan’s primary site had a self-signed TLS certificate, and the linked Style Media domain did not resolve.

Additional opened discovery/player resources: [Armenia News radio page](https://armenianews.org/radio/) and [its public JS](https://armenianews.org/assets/index-D_k_l5PV.js), [Armblog radio](https://radio.armblog.net/) and [its script](https://radio.armblog.net/script.js), [Media Initiatives radio directory](https://mediainitiatives.am/en/radio-en/) (curl 403), [Radioplayer](https://radioplayer.am), [Fama player script](https://player.radiofama.am/assets/js/aio-radio.min.js), [Fama jPlayer library](https://www.radiofama.am/wp-content/themes/radiofama/js/jPlayerRadio.js?ver=6.9.7), and [Caster.fm embed script](https://corscdn.caster.fm/freeplayer/FreePlanPlayerEmbed.js). Armblog’s script did not yield an immediately readable station inventory. Guessed Fama/about and Jazz/Mariam subpages that failed or lacked relevant information were not treated as evidence of closure. All candidate sources are listed above; a listed discovery pointer explicitly described as unopened is not claimed as a read primary page.

### Complete endpoint audit

Used the imported bounded project probe helper without catalog refresh: public-address pinning, valid TLS on all redirects, HTTP 200/206, MP3/AAC/Ogg and 4096 sample bytes. Same-host HTTPS alternatives were tested for HTTP-listed feeds; no insecure audio requests. Status 0 does not identify geoblocking, TLS cause or permanent closure. HLS, theme samples, country-unverified discovery-only leads and third-party relay-only URLs were not tested as direct audio.

### Duplicate review and next visit

Compared original and resolved endpoints globally against catalog, supplements and every earlier ledger run. Conservative review keys normalize default ports, percent encoding, trailing slashes, Zeno/Surfernetwork pool hosts by stream ID, RadioMast pool hosts by station UUID and myradiostream path-based port proxies. Signed/tracking queries are ignored only for duplicate review and preserved in actual probe evidence. Massive’s / and /stream and MAS’s /live and /stream are grouped with their known existing station URLs. Canal 90’s resolved RadioBoss mount is the existing feed, not a new addition. Gozadera’s two passing sources and Magic/Blue variants produce one record per service. The five explicitly named VIP mounts remain five channels. Similarly named unrelated global VIP stations were not merged by name. No ready candidate matches previous ledger audio URLs or catalog feeds.

Important findings: Radio Tropical’s own announcement pauses programming from March 2, 2026; passing directory audio is therefore held pending primary resumption/ownership evidence. University Shopa.Stream is explicitly documented but its published radio.co embed returns 404. Massive’s old domain is expired although its catalog stream still passes. Mega’s former site currently contains generic radio articles. Government frequency names are sometimes old: review Massive/Hot, Blue/Wavez, Radio Aruba/La Kalle, Hit 90.7/Caliente/Hit 94 and Galactica/Oldies rather than inferring same or different programming solely from frequencies. Bo Guia’s guide points to an unidentified worker relay; no direct compatible endpoint was verified.

Follow-ups: resolve Shopa.Stream, Fresh, Bo Guia, Hit 94, Easy and Power’s failed/obsolete players; seek supported direct alternatives for Heart, Cool and X FM HLS; follow Dushi’s primary country evidence and distinguish Curaçao namesakes; verify the additional internet/community/religious leads listed above. Pursue current Radio Latina and Voz di Aruba services and confirm whether legacy government brands survive independently. Expand immigrant/minority-language coverage beyond the Spanish/Papiamento/English evidence found; no separately evidenced Portuguese or Haitian-Creole domestic station was established. The absence of verified feeds does not prove that none exist.

Additional source access: opened [Curadise](https://curadise.fm/), [Online Radio Box Aruba](https://onlineradiobox.com/aw/), [University livestream](https://www.ua.aw/livestream/), the broadcaster sites and exact primary player resources in candidate sources above. Generic directory search results informed additional named leads but are not represented as complete operator audits. The Aruba government station pages and all Listen2Aruba detail URLs are explicitly preserved above. Primary sites that timed out or returned 403 were not bypassed. Web retrieval of Radio Tropical exposed its announcement despite direct curl failure. The university page was successfully fetched directly; one later web-tool retry timed out. Probe success is point-in-time audio transport verification, not worldwide or every-browser decoding.

These are point-in-time strict HTTPS audio transport checks with the project helper imported without running its catalog refresh. Status 0 is an unresolved connection failure, not evidence of closure or geographic blocking. HTTP-only directory URLs were tested using their same-host HTTPS equivalent. ### Duplicate review, limitations and next visit

Compared all original and resolved candidate endpoints globally against catalog, supplements and all earlier ledger URLs. Review keys normalize scheme, default ports, percent encoding, trailing slashes and tracking queries; actual probe URLs remain intact. Streamtheworld pool/redirect callsigns, radio.co station IDs, First Nations path/port proxies, myradiostream port proxies and XRN pool/quality variants were reviewed conservatively. Station evidence groups Noongar's 7013/8028, PAKAM's 7001/8004, Waringarri's 7023/8048 and 4RR's old Bullant/current Streamtheworld feeds. These are one service per station, not new stations per quality/host. 3KND, Waringarri, 4RR, Cherbourg, Radio MAMA, TEABBA, 2MCE, Ten FM, Rete Italia/Niche 1 and three XRN services are already represented. No ready proposal matches an earlier ledger or catalog feed under these checks.

A country-label review is needed for 24/7 Continuous Music: the exact feed already exists under Sweden (`SE`), while the operator's own site identifies CueLights as Australian. Preserve the existing record for review rather than adding a second feed. New 4RR transport is also recorded as a replacement lead for an existing service.

Some official sites returned 403 (Noongar, 6DBY, 3ZZZ, 4EB, Edge), 429 (2SER, Nova), DNS failures (7RPH's old domain, Aboriginal Broadcasting's former domain), or timeout (Collie). The old PAW /radio path returned 404. indigiTUBE URLs for PAW, Wilcannia, Angurugu, Umbakumba and Tjuma Pulka returned HTML, so those geographically valuable leads remain unresolved. 6PRK's own current published endpoint returned 404. Ngaarda's old Mixlr link returned 404, but its official ListenLive callsign resolved to passing audio; Black Star's currently linked iHeart player likewise provided a working replacement. Radio 1RPH's official alternatives both failed the project check. CueLights Radical FM returned 401 and Noughties Now returned 404; other explicitly named network channels passed. A published extension such as .aac does not override the actual returned MIME evidence.

ABC's [July 21, 2026 distribution notice](https://help.abc.net.au/hc/en-us/articles/15071793950607-Changes-to-ABC-Radio-Live-Streams-on-Third-Party-Platforms) documents changes affecting third-party access since February 2026. It does not establish that every ABC endpoint is unusable. SBS's current primary player provides HLS URLs, with literal .m3u variants retained where published; these were not tested or counted as direct-audio passes. Archived podcast MP3s on network pages were not treated as live stations. The ARDS /yolngu-radio/ URL currently resolves to a merchandise page that nevertheless includes the broadcaster's own Northeast Arnhem Land service description; stream evidence comes from the First Nations locator.

Next Australia visit: continue the unreviewed Radio Browser inventory systematically; enumerate ABC regional services and current distribution URLs; review SBS direct-audio alternatives; expand Hit/Triple M, ARN and Nova regional/commercial coverage; resolve PAW, Wilcannia, Groote Eylandt, Tjuma Pulka, 6PRK, Wangki, Ngarralinyi and BBM current players; check 2SER, 2NUR, Edge and the print-access radio networks. Review 3ZZZ Sports/DAB, Global, CBAA unique DAB channels, minority-language broadcasters, 6EBA's current operational status and additional independent internet stations. English searches plus primary Indigenous station metadata were used; no dedicated Indigenous-language search was performed. Territorial coverage follows the separate ISO rows, so external territories will receive their own scheduled turns. Failed discovery is not proof that no station exists.

The initial checkpoint and earlier logs are preserved. No catalog/supplement integration, full refresh, build or publication was performed. Checklist verification: 250 unique entries including Palestine, Western Sahara and Kosovo. Next scheduled country: Austria (`AT`).

The [Kronehit public player](https://www.kronehit.at/) uses a read-only public websocket at `wss://www.kronehit.at/api/_socket/`, documented in the retrieved player loader. It returned 13 named channel configurations, including duplicate/variant entries and existing partner services. No login or authenticated account action was used. Only channel identity and public live URLs are relevant; podcasts and advertising resources were not treated as live radio. Unfilled listener/consent tracking placeholders were removed from probe URLs, with the original template preserved below.

### Duplicate review and remaining work

Compared original and resolved endpoints globally against the catalog, supplements and all earlier ledger runs. Review keys normalize protocol, default ports, percent encoding, trailing slashes and tracking queries; actual request URLs are preserved in evidence. Known ORF quality variants, Laut.fm player/stream aliases, Streamtheworld callsigns and provider pools were compared conservatively. Campus & City Radio’s old cr944.at:50443 and current stream.cr944.at feeds, AGORA’s old/current player hosts, AIR’s /128 and /stream quality players, Super80s spelling/query variants and the ORF Campus university program were tied to existing services by primary station evidence. Kronehit digital and UKW both passed; one main-station proposal is retained pending proof of distinct programming. Most Wanted is explicitly a separately named channel. Super80s1/rwr1/eurodance1 remain same-brand variants rather than additional unverified stations. WEANARISCH’s passing feed already exists with a spelling variation. No ready record matches any prior ledger or catalog audio URL under these checks.

Findings: FRO and Freistadt have current secure streams absent from the catalog. B138’s old webstream host failed resolution, while the exact official Streamerr embed exposed a passing replacement. OÖNow’s public streams.json redirects to a working provider endpoint. Nostalgie’s embedded Radioplayer URL returned 404; the Austrian directory player supplies a current NRJ endpoint, distinct from France/Germany namesakes. Radio Maria’s current host supports both quality feeds. Radio Harmonie’s official page supplies a working replacement for its old cartwall address. Radio Radieschen is independently identified by its university and has a passing current stream; Vienna’s former NJOY branding must not be conflated with NJOY Steiermark.

Failures and limitations: Radio SOL, Radio Osttirol and the Radieschen homepage returned 403; old SOL/Radieschen player paths returned 404. The old erf.at site had a certificate failure and AustrianPowerRadio’s domain had a certificate-name mismatch; no TLS bypass. Stadtradio Krems and Achwelle timed out, and radio.achwelle.at did not resolve. Old Ypsilon, ARBÖ, SOL, Osttirol and parish stream checks failed. Styrialounge returned 401 and Vogal FM 502. All three published Radio Fantasy player variants failed. A passing 28Radio feed is held because Austrian origin was not established; its API timezone does not establish a country either. One World Radio carriage in Kronehit similarly does not establish an Austrian-local service. Directory labels for other foreign-looking feeds remain uncertain rather than being reassigned. TV/HLS entries are excluded from direct-audio radio proposals. ORF HLS/surround variants, podcast MP3s, Wix audio clips and website/player pages are not claimed as verified live feeds.

The ORF national and nine regional services, Slovenski spored and Ö1 Campus are present in the directory/catalog triage. Primary FM4 guidance still publishes its direct endpoints, and a fresh FM4 check passed. University of Vienna Radio Campus is scheduled programming within Ö1 Campus. AGORA and MORA provide primary minority-language/community evidence; language lists are left empty where exact current programming languages were not independently transcribed. German/English searches were completed, but deeper Slovenian, Burgenland Croatian, Hungarian, Romani and migrant-language research remains for the next sweep.

Next Austria visit: resolve Ypsilon, ARBÖ, Radio SOL, Osttirol, parish radio, Styrialounge, Vogal FM, Achwelle and Radio Fantasy; verify AustrianPowerRadio and 28Radio origin; clarify ERF/NOW legacy services and cross-border South Tyrol provenance. Continue unmatched directory groups and official DAB additions, especially Antenne Hit, Radio MediaMarkt, arabella MAGIC, Antenne Wien/Niederösterreich and ROCK FM Österreich. Determine local production versus foreign carriage for Beats, Klassik Radio, Sout al khaleej and One World Radio. Expand official 88.6, Arabella, Antenne, Life Radio and Welle regional/online channel enumeration beyond directory comparisons, and distinguish their meaningful programming variants. Refresh this run’s ready candidates against the catalog on any integration or next visit.

Preserved all earlier logs and the initial checkpoint. No catalog/supplement change, full refresh, build or publication was performed. Validated all 250 unique country/territory codes, including Palestine, Western Sahara and Kosovo. Next scheduled country: Azerbaijan (`AZ`).

### Final endpoint evidence

Bounded project checker with normal TLS, public-address DNS pinning, supported direct MP3/AAC/Ogg MIME and 4,096-byte samples. A status-0 failure has no established cause beyond connection/check failure; it does not prove geoblocking or closure. The one accidental HTTP checker input was rejected before any insecure fetch; its HTTPS counterpart was already tested in the initial batch. Passing redirects containing short-lived provider tokens are retained only as evidence; proposals use stable original public URLs.

### Final endpoint evidence

Fresh bounded project checks required valid TLS on every redirect, a public pinned address, HTTP 200/206, supported MP3/AAC/Ogg MIME and at least 4,096 bytes. No TLS, login, 401/403 or geographic restrictions were bypassed. A status-0 failure has no established cause beyond connection/check failure and does not prove closure or geoblocking. The unsupported MMS input was rejected locally without an MMS network request. Provider redirect tokens are short-lived public playback evidence; proposed records use stable original URLs. Successful probes do not prove browser decoding or worldwide availability.

### Duplicate review, limitations and next leads

Compared original and resolved URLs globally with every catalog station, the supplemental file and all prior ledger runs. Review keys normalize URL encoding, protocol/default ports and trailing slash aliases while preserving functional query parameters such as Reliastream’s mp=/stream. Securenet ice-host variants are grouped by exact call sign; Zeno and Surfernetwork redirects by stream ID; StreamTheWorld redirects by channel filename; RadioBOSS /stream/186 and port 8186/stream by account. Different Streamcomedia ports/mounts remain distinct. Proposed feeds have no matching catalog or prior-ledger keys and no duplicate proposal keys. Antenna Web’s globally cataloged /8066/stream is not a new Bahamas service. MP3Islam was already held for origin during Azerbaijan. Radio Browser duplicate Guardian and Bahamian or Nuttin rows are retained under their existing feeds.

ZNS’s own page identifies four program services: National Voice in Nassau, Inspiration in Nassau, Power in Freeport and The Light in Freeport. The public player HTML and linked JavaScript describe the read-only playerConfig endpoint and how streamAddress/defaultMountUrl form the audio URL. Three working current feeds came through those official player configurations. Power’s primary button incorrectly links the National Voice page; its distinct current port 8004 feed came from published Zeno metadata and passed normally over HTTPS. Do not count the AM/FM relays as additional programs. Turning Point’s official linked configuration similarly recovered its current port 8026 feed from the failed legacy directory address.

Primary Gospel and Vibes pages expose current working audio directly. HOT and 100 JAMZ public Securenet players expose current call signs. Station-owned public Facebook metadata established More94 and KISS96 Nassau identity when other pages were unavailable. Prayse’s directory Facebook link resolves to a personal profile and provides no station identity proof; its passing audio remains held. Big105’s business promotion alone is insufficient proof of exact audio origin. Vogue Play and Station Beta also need geographic verification. KISS’s published HTTPS port 80 endpoint passed valid TLS, as did its default HTTPS-port equivalent; this is one stream.

The publisher description and regulator entry together identify Smooth Radio Network / Kingdom Vibes 95.9 in Green Castle, Eleuthera. Radio Alisnet’s publisher explicitly states Bahamas; its Marsh Harbour/Abaco location is still secondary-only. Radio Bérée’s primary page explicitly identifies Haitian community radio in Nassau. Its two published Zeno mounts failed; some Dribbcast playlists returned 404 or connection reset, and remaining primary-linked playlist variants need follow-up. Do not infer that it stopped broadcasting. Zeno’s Glory and Joy entries expose working audio but provide insufficient current primary operator identity corroboration in this pass; historical URCA and sponsor results are follow-up evidence, not current license/operator proof. The Blaze publisher describes an Exuma community service; its legacy audio fails and its relationship to Exuma Breeze remains unresolved.

The 40-page URCA register includes broadcasting and other communications licensees. The inspected Broadcasting Corporation page includes radio and television assignments; school/college 450 MHz entries are not automatically broadcast radio. SNL in Matthew Town, Smooth in Green Castle and Splash in Spanish Wells provide island-specific leads beyond Nassau. Keep Splash’s conflicting directory Nassau address, New Wave/Y98 location ambiguity, Mix/Intercity 102.1 and DKM/Glory mapping unresolved until primary evidence establishes the current service. Shared FM frequencies across islands do not prove a common program.

Next Bahamas visit: refresh all ready feeds before any catalog integration; identify current Glory, Joy, Prayse and Big105 primary operators/players; recover Radio Bérée’s remaining linked Dribbcast playlists, Dove, Love97, Island102.9, Peace107.5, Radio Abaco, Y98, Classical98.1, Exuma Breeze/The Blaze, WORD88.3, Infolight and Splash. Pursue Andros Praise88.5, Long Island106.1 and Inagua106.1, Lyfe/Libète, remaining URCA licensee brands and university/community production. Follow unvisited Zeno country-page leads Da Groove/WSoul, GBTube, Radio Cooteeca/Oldies, Rudon Media Group, RV7Underground, SKYE Radio and other local web stations, verifying domestic versus diaspora origin; generic BBC or international religious network entries are not automatically Bahamas stations. ### Final endpoint evidence

All results below come from fresh bounded project checks with normal certificate validation, public-address DNS pinning, supported direct audio MIME, HTTP 200/206 and 4,096-byte samples. The 46 inputs include public HLS/playlist URLs and one accidentally extracted bare Streamlock host; they are not 46 candidate audio services. A status 0 failure establishes no cause beyond connection/check failure, and does not prove closure or geoblocking. No HTTP audio, authentication/TLS bypass, proxy/geographic circumvention or restricted player access was used. Short-lived public provider tokens remain evidence only; proposals retain stable originals. These checks do not prove browser decoding or worldwide availability.

### Duplicate review, limitations and next leads

Compared every original and resolved URL globally with the current catalog, all seven records in the supplemental file, and all prior ledger runs. Keys normalize protocol/default ports, trailing slash and URL encoding; retain functional parameters such as mp=/1; remove only known playback tracking/token parameters and an empty numeric cache-buster. Aiir host variants normalize by stream ID, RadioJar by station ID, Qurango primary/backup hosts by mount, Zeno/Surfernetwork by stream ID and StreamTheWorld by final channel path. Source URLs and actual redirects remain intact. The five proposals have no matching catalog or prior-ledger audio keys and no duplicate proposal keys. AFN’s existing MP3/AAC formats, Voice of Ummah’s new primary /listen/vou path, BFBS’s AAC/MP3 alternatives, and Radio Bahrain’s Aiir host variants are grouped by explicitly supported service identity; alternate formats do not become extra stations.

Six groups have existing global feed matches: AFN Bahrain, Live FM, Voice of Ummah, Qurango salma, Antenna Web and Quran for the Soul. Their existing country labels are not independently validated by a URL match. Monte Carlo Doualiya is separately excluded from Bahrain proposals because its operator explicitly identifies Paris origin, regardless of its global duplicate match. The CBS93.9/Yucatec Maya row is an inconsistent foreign-feed assignment and excluded. Generic Qurango commentary/reciter streams and MP3Islam lack primary Bahrain origin evidence, even when they pass. Quran 106.1 is a separate public broadcaster service; do not substitute generic Quran channels or RadioJar IDs for it.

Radio Bahrain’s exact current stream was extracted from its official /player/ page. Suno’s public Base64 player configuration names its 87.6 service and exact suno876 mount; both station and operator distinguish Bahrain from Qatar Suno 91.7 and Olive. Plus FM’s app publisher links its official web player, which publishes the same itworkscdn9026 feed seen in the directory. BFBS’s named regional player publishes AAC/MP3 for Bahrain; the operator also documents services at Bahrain’s UK Naval Support Facility. The individual production locations of its shared network programs were not established. Mirchi’s current About page still describes Bahrain operations, and its distinct BAH_HIN_GSTAAC stream passes. Its historical radio routes returned 404; even a route found in the public JS bundle was obsolete, while /bahrain/ returned generic entertainment content. Do not claim an exact current primary-player linkage for Mirchi beyond the recorded identity-plus-directory evidence. Reconfirm at integration.

The public Arabic 102.3, FM 93.3, Traditional 95.0, Quran 106.1 and Youth 98.4 stream URLs respond as HLS. They remain unsupported, and no segment playback was claimed. The old English 96.5 HLS returns 404, while the current official Aiir feed works. Ministry pages repeatedly returned 405 and the web reader also failed; requests did not bypass that restriction. This limits recovery of direct audio for public services, Tarab and Arabian Gulf Radio. Historical frequency variants and DAB/FM relays do not establish separate online programs. Sports television audio and foreign BBC, DW, Emarat, Sawa and Sout Al Khaleej reception are recorded as follow-up or relay leads, not automatic Bahrain stations.

Live FM’s existing endpoint failed in this pass despite matching its primary site. The primary launch report establishes Isa Town production and multilingual community remit; failure is not evidence of closure. BMC’s primary pages establish its Bahrain identity but no live stream replacement; its current content includes news and video items. Its site also has a stray Melbourne map-template link, which was not used as geographic evidence. Radio Manna’s primary replacement passes, but its team description, Kerala label and Indian/Bahraini contacts leave current origin unresolved. Manama onlayn’s blog supplies audio but no adequate operator/location evidence; the generic Adhari page similarly does not establish a distinct local broadcaster. NRVoice, Voice of Malankara and Shabakat Nur streams failed and need origin verification. Islamic Bulletin/Quran for the Soul has conflicting country/channel labels; passing Mixlr audio does not resolve them.

University research found training, faculty interviews and programs on established Bahrain Radio, not a verified independent continuous campus station. Only the Ahlia college page was successfully fetched locally; University of Bahrain outreach returned 406, while web search provided primary excerpts. No absence claim is made. Additional Zeno country-page entries for already represented public/forces/Ummah services and BFBS Brunei were seen but not fully audited; a country listing is insufficient evidence of local origin.

Next Bahrain visit: refresh the five ready proposals and Live FM’s failed check; recover Mirchi’s current primary player route, Ministry direct-audio options, Tarab and Arabian Gulf Radio; resolve BMC’s deleted Fastcast feed and current Manna base; verify Manama onlayn, DJ Plus, NRVoice, Malankara and Shabakat Nur provenance. Pursue any newly evidenced university/community station, and compare local relays with network programming before adding a country-specific feed. Keep unverified geographic labels and historical frequency aliases explicit.

Preserved all earlier logs and both checkpoints. No catalog or supplemental changes, full refresh, build, release or automation changes. Checklist validated for 250 unique countries/territories, including Palestine, Western Sahara and Kosovo. Next scheduled country: Bangladesh (`BD`).

### Sources opened and coverage

Used English and Bengali searches across national and regional public radio, commercial networks, local/community and university stations, internet-only music/drama/religious services, and minority-language programming. The primary regional Rangamati page explicitly lists Bengali, Chakma, Tripura, Marma and Tanchangya news. The Naf and ACLAB primary web results describe local/Rohingya community services. These are programming facts, not separate new radio stations for each language.

Fetched 14 regional government homepages. Older Dhaka/Sylhet live links returned 404, but national navigation yielded 33 current named service pages. All 33 were retrieved and their port-specific HTTP DigitalSynapse player links attempted over HTTPS on the same host/port/path. All 33 HTTPS player-page requests failed; these are webpage fetch attempts, separate from the 74 actual stream-check inputs. The original government links remain in each candidate’s primaryPlayerPages evidence. Two long Bengali commercial-page URLs initially collided in local truncated filenames; both were fetched again under unique hashed names before final extraction. Final page evidence uses the corrected files.

Radio Browser, Online Radio Box and Radio-Bangladesh.com/Radoxo are discovery metadata, not proof of official operator control. Primary site/player or publisher text establishes the ready candidates’ identity/country. Six Betar proposals combine primary government service identity with named passing directory streams; direct equivalence to the old primary port-specific players was not established. This limitation is explicit for catalog review. A generic Betar Zeno relay remains unassigned rather than becoming another public service.

The public fetch manifest below includes failed requests, exploratory paths, directory profiles and publicly served player scripts. Empty files are failures, not evidence that a station is closed. The Naf, ACLAB, BRAC/Pollikontho, DIU, KUET, UNESCO and historical AMARC/CEMCA references also appeared in web-reader/search results; only references present in the fetch manifest were retrieved as local full pages. ### Duplicate review, limitations and next leads

Compared every original and resolved stream URL globally against current catalog records, all seven supplements and all prior ledger runs. Normalization handles protocol/default ports, trailing slash, URL encoding and known playback tokens; functional proxy query parameters remain significant. Zeno/Surfernetwork host variants normalize by stream ID, including the known optional .mp3 suffix; MyRadioStream /listen.mp3 and /; on the same host/port normalize together. Qurango aliases normalize by mount. All proposed selected original/final keys are absent from catalog, supplements, prior ledger and other proposals. This is URL and supported service-identity review, not audio fingerprinting. Similar station names alone do not prove duplicate programming.

Bhumi’s current primary ybf1umk1k18uv feed is already cataloged under India, while another Bhumi feed is in Bangladesh. Record the country conflict for later correction; neither is a new addition. Foorti’s catalog API works, while old IP fails and a directory Zeno alternative works. Goongoon’s two paths and Shadhin’s tokenized/stable Zeno forms are retained within their service groups. Hemel and Today each have a current primary stream plus an older passing directory stream; only the current primary is proposed. Sixteen groups match existing global records, which does not independently validate those records’ country assignments.

Purbakantho’s current blog states a Netrakona address, but the player script it links plays Bushra’s mount. Its own separately directory-labeled feed passes but remains held for contradictory identity. Theater and Dawah lack adequate production-country evidence despite passing audio. FnF’s three primary channels pass, but production origin remains unresolved; its Bollywood channel is already globally cataloged in India. Generic Quran and health streams are not assigned domestic origin solely from language or directory metadata. The generic Betar Zeno relay is not mapped to a specific official service.

Mahananda, Padma, Nalta and Bushra have primary direct-player linkage. BU RADiO’s source bundle publishes a working live fallback; the core API root returns 530, so possible runtime override was not verified. BUET and Meghna return 401. Chilmari’s publisher configuration indicates protected streaming and server not ready; no attempt was made to bypass it. Radio Naf’s site returns 406 to curl while the web reader supplies current station/operator text; its direct player remains unresolved. Ekattor and Carnival’s former domains serve unrelated legal and gambling pages. Capital’s current religious content is insufficient to verify its old directory stream. None of these results proves permanent closure.

Government navigation contains inconsistent historical labels: the link labeled Dhaka FM 102 points to a page slug describing Dhaka Kha 819, and the link labeled FM 106 points to a slug describing FM 102. These conflicts are retained rather than silently resolved. Regional AM/FM services have their own evidence entries; no proof of identical or different programming is inferred from frequency alone. Primary Bandarbans AM/FM ports differ, and only the named directory FM proxy passed. Rangamati minority-language services still lack compatible audio in this pass. The national anthem MP3 on government pages, Padma archived programs, SoundCloud episodes and television/social embeds were not counted as live streams.

Next Bangladesh visit: refresh all 13 proposals, map the six Betar directory streams to current official playback configuration, resolve the generic Zeno relay and remaining 27 government AM/FM player pages, and check the Dhaka frequency-label conflicts. Revisit Purbakantho/Bushra identity, Hemel/Today legacy programming, FnF origin, Dawah/Theater provenance, BU runtime settings, BUET/Meghna access failures, Chilmari/Naf players and Dhaka/Jago/Spice replacements. Follow campus KUET/DIU leads and community stations Mukti, Lokobetar, Krishi Radio, Pollikontho, Jhenuk, Sundarban, Bikrampur, Barendra, Boral and Sagor Dwip; those names arose from historical/community source results but were not individually verified as current online stations. Radio Amber’s newly discovered IP failed and its primary player remains a lead. BNNRC root was retrieved but its old network route returned 404; recover the current network directory on a later sweep. Do not describe these remaining leads as absent stations.

Preserved all previous run logs and Bangladesh checkpoints. No catalog/supplement writes, full refresh, build, release or automation changes. The country checklist remains 250 unique entries, including Palestine, Western Sahara and Kosovo. Next scheduled country: Barbados (`BB`).

### Sources opened and coverage

Used English with local Barbados/Bajan terms, the national broadcaster, commercial networks and station-owned websites, faith/community outlets, Barbados Community College and UWI Cave Hill references, tourism and internet-only radio. Search results and the historical regulator table covered BBS, Faith, education/emergency radio, planned Power Radio and foreign reception leads. The register webpage has an expired certificate, so its searchable primary text was used as historical identity evidence, not a claim that current transport or operations were verified. PDFs appearing in search results (UWI reports, regulator2018, Commonwealth2026 and Internews2021) were not fully opened/rendered this pass; their excerpts are leads rather than full-document audits.

Retrieved 22 Radio Browser rows, 17 distinct ORB homepage players and 16 linked station profiles, plus CITA’s separately discovered ORB profile. Four ORB items are external SecureNet player pages, not direct audio. Station directories are discovery aids and may mislabel country, frequency, genre or operational status. CBC’s current primary player configuration was read from JSON embedded in its HTML. CITA links TuneIn s180740, whose public Tune.ashx metadata supplied the checked Asura AAC stream. Pirate FM’s primary site links Mira’s public player, whose downloadPlaylistUri provided the two checked mounts. One Worldwide’s primary site links the exact RadioKing redirect that resolves to its directory stream.

Starcom main/VOB pages and Power Slam return403 to curl. Y103 and the regulator webpage have expired TLS certificates; Y103 also timed out in a separate web-reader open. No certificate or access bypass was attempted. Other failures, guessed/obsolete paths and missing DNS are retained in the manifest. The Antenna Web homepage unexpectedly delivered MPEG audio until the bounded fetch timeout (981,099 bytes), so it was not parsed as an identity page or counted as another successful project audio check. No network origin was inferred from it.

### Final endpoint evidence

Fresh bounded probe_endpoint results are recorded below. Success requires normal TLS validation, HTTPS redirects, public-address DNS pinning, HTTP 200/206, supported MP3/AAC/Ogg MIME and at least 4,096 sample bytes. One NBG input retained its published HTTP scheme by extraction mistake; the checker rejected it before any network request. Its separately attempted HTTPS upgrade also failed. Thus there are 45 checker inputs, not 45 HTTPS network requests. No insecure audio request, login/TLS bypass or geographic circumvention was performed.

CBC itself publishes three Surfmusic HTTPS relay URLs with an HTTP upstream address in the query. The checker verified the public HTTPS relay response only; it cannot establish transport inside the relay or independently confirm the relay’s upstream connection. These primary-selected relays were not constructed as a workaround by this research. By contrast, Radoxo’s third-party Tunzilla wrap of the failed NBG origin was noted but neither probed nor adopted.

A status 0/check failure does not establish closure or geoblocking. Playlist/webpage availability is not a direct-audio pass. Successful checks do not establish every-browser decoding, worldwide availability or whether alternate mounts carry identical programming. Expiring Zeno redirects remain evidence only.
